subject: Ethernet II frame, untagged vs 802.1Q tagged

source.locator: IEEE 802.3 MAC frame format (Clause 3: Destination Address, Source Address, Length/Type, MAC Client Data, Pad, FCS) together with IEEE 802.1Q C-VLAN tag format (Clause 9.6: TPID 0x8100 + TCI = PCP/DEI/VID)

authored.protocol: source-first: the author agent read only the source standards and never saw the .fd file

questions.ask: In an untagged Ethernet II frame, which field comes immediately after the Source Address field, in on-the-wire order?
questions.tests: field order: Source Address is directly followed by EtherType/Length, not by the payload or FCS
questions.source_locator: IEEE 802.3, Clause 3.1, MAC frame format field order
questions.answer: The EtherType/Length field (2 bytes) comes immediately after the Source Address field.

questions.ask: How many bytes long is each of the Destination Address and Source Address fields in an Ethernet II frame?
questions.tests: field size: both MAC address fields are 6 bytes (48 bits) each
questions.answer: Each address field is 6 bytes (48 bits) long.

questions.ask: Where in the frame is the 802.1Q VLAN tag inserted, relative to the Source Address and EtherType/Length fields?
questions.tests: insertion point: the tag sits between Source Address and EtherType/Length, not before Source Address or after the payload
questions.answer: The tag is inserted immediately after the Source Address field and before the EtherType/Length field.

questions.ask: What is the total size, in bytes, of the 802.1Q tag inserted into the frame?
questions.tests: tag size: the whole tag (TPID + TCI) is 4 bytes, not just the TCI or VID alone
questions.answer: The 802.1Q tag is 4 bytes (32 bits) total: 2 bytes of TPID plus 2 bytes of TCI.

questions.ask: The Tag Control Information (TCI) part of the 802.1Q tag is made up of three subfields. Name them and give the bit width of each.
questions.tests: tag content structure: TCI decomposes into PCP (3 bits), DEI (1 bit), VID (12 bits)
questions.answer: PCP (Priority Code Point), 3 bits; DEI (Drop Eligible Indicator), 1 bit; and VID (VLAN Identifier), 12 bits.

questions.ask: What 2-byte hexadecimal value occupies the first two bytes of the 802.1Q tag, marking the frame as tagged?
questions.tests: tag content: the TPID value that distinguishes a tagged frame from an untagged one where EtherType would otherwise sit

questions.ask: What is the allowed size range, in bytes, of the payload (MAC Client Data) field in a standard untagged Ethernet frame?
questions.tests: payload size range distinct from overall frame size or address field sizes
questions.source_locator: IEEE 802.3, Clause 3.1/4.2.3, Data field length bounds (min frame size 64 bytes drives the 46-byte floor; max 1500-byte MTU is the ceiling)
questions.answer: The payload (Data field) ranges from 46 bytes to 1500 bytes.

questions.ask: Besides the FCS field itself, what part of the transmitted frame is excluded from the FCS's CRC calculation?
questions.tests: coverage: FCS covers Destination Address through Data/Pad, but not the leading Preamble/SFD
questions.source_locator: IEEE 802.3, Clause 3.1, FCS field, CRC computation range
questions.answer: The Preamble and Start Frame Delimiter (SFD) at the start of the frame are excluded from the FCS's CRC calculation.
